Topics.Title: Introduction to PreseMaker's Publish Feature
Topics.Summary: An overview of what the publish feature does in PreseMaker and why it is used to assemble course modules into a browsable website.

Elements.Title: What Is the Publish Feature?
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker's publish feature is a built-in tool that assembles a course's individual modules into a single, cohesive browsable website.
Elements.Notes: Think of it as the final packaging step that transforms separately authored modules into a unified site learners can navigate.

Items.Text: The publish feature collects all course modules and organizes them into a structured website format.
It automates the assembly process, removing the need to manually link or arrange module files.
The result is a browsable site where learners can move between modules without additional configuration.

Elements.Title: The Role of Each Module's HTML Index
Elements.BodyText: Each module in PreseMaker has an HTML index file that serves as its landing page within the published website.
Elements.Notes: The HTML index is the entry point for a module — the first page a learner sees when navigating to that section of the course site.

Items.Text: Every module contributes one HTML index file, which acts as its dedicated starting page.
The publish feature uses these index files as the anchor points when building the site's navigation structure.
Ensuring each module has a properly formed HTML index is essential for the published site to function correctly.

Elements.Title: How Publishing Refreshes Module Content
Elements.BodyText: Before building the site, PreseMaker's publish feature refreshes each module's HTML index to ensure it reflects the most current content.
Elements.Notes: This refresh step is automatic and occurs as part of the publish process, so learners always see up-to-date material.

Items.Text: Publishing triggers a content refresh so that any recent edits or additions are captured before the site is assembled.
This prevents outdated versions of a module from appearing in the live website.
The refresh step ensures consistency between what authors have created and what learners ultimately browse.

Elements.Title: Why the Publish Feature Is Used
Elements.BodyText: The publish feature exists to give course authors a reliable, repeatable way to deliver a complete and current course website to learners.
Elements.Notes: Without a dedicated publish step, authors would need to manually update links, re-export files, and verify content currency across every module.

Items.Text: It consolidates multiple modules into one browsable experience, reducing complexity for both authors and learners.
By bundling assembly and content refresh into a single action, it saves time and reduces the risk of publishing errors.
It provides a consistent output format, making the course site predictable and easy to maintain over time.

Topics.Title: Understanding Module HTML Index Pages
Topics.Summary: Explains the role of each module's HTML index file as its landing page and how it represents the module's content within the published site.

Elements.Title: What Is a Module HTML Index Page?
Elements.BodyText: Each module in a course website has a dedicated HTML index file that acts as its primary entry point.
Elements.Notes: Think of it like the front door of each module — it is the first page a learner lands on when navigating to that module within the published site.

Items.Text: The HTML index file is automatically associated with its module and carries the module's name and identity within the site structure.
It is a standard HTML file, meaning it can be opened and viewed in any web browser without special software.
Every module has its own distinct index file, keeping each module's content self-contained and independently accessible.

Elements.Title: The Landing Page Role of the Index File
Elements.BodyText: The module HTML index page serves as the landing page — the starting point learners reach when they navigate to a specific module.
Elements.Notes: In a multi-module course site, each module's index page provides a consistent entry point, making navigation predictable and organized for learners.

Items.Text: When a learner clicks on a module link within the course website, they are directed to that module's HTML index page first.
The index page orients the learner by presenting the module's content in a structured, accessible way.
Acting as a landing page, the index file anchors the module's position within the broader course site hierarchy.

Elements.Title: How the Index Page Represents Module Content
Elements.BodyText: The HTML index file reflects the current state of a module's content, serving as a snapshot of what that module contains.
Elements.Notes: If content within a module is updated, the index page must also be updated to accurately represent those changes to learners visiting the site.

Items.Text: The index page surfaces the module's key content elements, giving learners an accurate representation of what the module includes.
Any content added, removed, or modified within a module should ultimately be reflected in the module's index page.
The index file bridges the raw module content and the published website, translating internal content into a browsable web page.

Elements.Title: Publishing Refreshes the HTML Index
Elements.BodyText: Using PreseMaker's publish feature automatically refreshes each module's HTML index file before the course site is built.
Elements.Notes: This refresh step is critical — it ensures that the published site always reflects the most recent version of each module's content rather than an outdated snapshot.

Items.Text: Each time the publish feature is run, PreseMaker regenerates the HTML index files to incorporate the latest module content.
Refreshing the index during publishing prevents outdated or mismatched content from appearing on the live course website.
The publish-and-refresh cycle ensures consistency between what is authored in the module and what learners see on the site.

Elements.Title: Index Pages Within the Site Structure
Elements.BodyText: Module HTML index pages are the building blocks that allow individual modules to integrate into the larger course website.
Elements.Notes: A well-structured course site relies on each module's index page being properly formed so that site-wide navigation and linking function correctly.

Items.Text: Each module's index page is linked from the course's main site navigation, enabling learners to browse between modules seamlessly.
The index files collectively form the navigable layer of the course website, with each representing one module's content area.
Proper index pages ensure the published site is coherent and that no module is orphaned or unreachable within the site structure.

Topics.Title: How Publishing Refreshes Module Content
Topics.Summary: Describes the process by which publishing updates each module's HTML index to reflect the most current content before the website is built.

Elements.Title: The Role of the HTML Index in Each Module
Elements.BodyText: Each module in PreseMaker has an HTML index file that serves as its landing page within the course website.
Elements.Notes: Think of the HTML index as the front door to a module — it is the first file a browser loads when a learner navigates to that module.

Items.Text: The HTML index file aggregates and represents all of the content belonging to its module.
When the course website is browsed, visitors arrive at a module's HTML index before accessing individual pieces of content.
Keeping this file current is essential for ensuring learners see accurate and complete module information.

Elements.Title: What Triggers a Content Refresh
Elements.BodyText: The publishing action in PreseMaker is the event that triggers a refresh of each module's HTML index.
Elements.Notes: A refresh does not happen automatically as content is edited; it is specifically initiated when the instructor or author invokes the publish feature.

Items.Text: Initiating the publish feature signals PreseMaker to scan each module for its most current content.
Any additions, edits, or deletions made to module content since the last publish are captured during this refresh step.
Without publishing, the HTML index may reflect outdated content from a previous build.

Elements.Title: How PreseMaker Updates the HTML Index
Elements.BodyText: During publishing, PreseMaker rewrites each module's HTML index to incorporate the latest content before assembling the full site.
Elements.Notes: This rewrite process ensures that the index is not simply appended to but is fully regenerated to reflect the current state of the module.

Items.Text: PreseMaker reads the current state of all content items within a module and regenerates the HTML index accordingly.
The regenerated index replaces the previous version, eliminating stale links or missing entries.
This step updates each module whose HTML index is out of date, so the published site reflects the latest content.

Elements.Title: Sequence: Refresh Before Build
Elements.BodyText: The content refresh of each module's HTML index is completed before the overall course website is built, ensuring the site is assembled from up-to-date files.
Elements.Notes: The deliberate ordering — refresh first, build second — means the website construction phase always works from accurate source files.

Items.Text: PreseMaker follows a defined sequence: update each module's HTML index first, then compile those indexes into the browsable website.
This ordering prevents the website build from using a mix of current and outdated module indexes.
Learners who access the published site can therefore trust that each module landing page reflects the most recent content.

Elements.Title: Impact on the Browsable Course Website
Elements.BodyText: Because each module's HTML index is refreshed before the site is built, the resulting browsable website accurately mirrors the current state of all course content.
Elements.Notes: This end-to-end consistency is the primary benefit of the publish-then-build workflow.

Items.Text: Learners navigating the site encounter module landing pages that list only current, valid content.
Instructors can confidently share or deploy the published site knowing it reflects their latest changes.
Any module-level updates made after the last publish will not appear on the live site until the publish feature is run again.

Topics.Title: Assembling Modules into a Course Website
Topics.Summary: Walks learners through the steps of combining individual course modules into a cohesive, browsable website structure using PreseMaker.

Elements.Title: Overview of the Course Website Assembly Process
Elements.BodyText: Assembling a course website in PreseMaker means combining multiple individual modules into a single, cohesive, browsable structure.
Elements.Notes: Think of each module as a chapter in a book; the course website is the bound volume that ties them all together.

Items.Text: PreseMaker's publish feature serves as the central tool for combining modules into a unified website.
The result is a browsable site where learners can navigate from one module to another seamlessly.
Understanding the overall process first helps prevent missteps when working through individual steps.

Elements.Title: The Role of Each Module's HTML Index File
Elements.BodyText: Every module in PreseMaker has an HTML index file that acts as its landing page within the larger course website.
Elements.Notes: The index file is automatically generated by PreseMaker and serves as the entry point learners reach when they navigate to that module.

Items.Text: The HTML index file is the first page a learner sees when they enter a specific module.
Each module's index file links to that module's individual lessons, topics, or assets.
Keeping index files current is essential so learners always land on accurate, up-to-date content.

Elements.Title: How Publishing Refreshes Module Content
Elements.BodyText: Before PreseMaker builds the full course site, it refreshes each module's HTML index to ensure the latest content is reflected.
Elements.Notes: This automatic refresh step prevents outdated information from appearing on the live site without requiring manual file updates.

Items.Text: Publishing triggers a refresh of every module's HTML index, incorporating any recent edits or additions.
This means the assembled website always represents the most current state of each module at the time of publishing.
Learners and instructors can trust that content visible on the site matches the latest saved version of each module.

Elements.Title: Using PreseMaker's Publish Feature to Build the Site
Elements.BodyText: The publish feature in PreseMaker is the primary mechanism for converting a collection of modules into a complete, navigable course website.
Elements.Notes: Locating and initiating the publish function correctly is a critical hands-on skill covered in this topic.

Items.Text: Learners must locate the publish feature within PreseMaker's interface before beginning the assembly process.
Initiating publish starts the sequence of refreshing module indexes and then compiling them into the site structure.
Completing the publish process produces a fully linked website ready for learner access.

Elements.Title: Ensuring a Cohesive Navigation Structure
Elements.BodyText: A well-assembled course website provides clear, consistent navigation so learners can move between modules without confusion.
Elements.Notes: PreseMaker handles much of the structural linking automatically, but understanding how modules connect helps instructors verify the site behaves as expected.

Items.Text: PreseMaker automatically generates navigation links between modules based on the order and structure defined in the course.
Instructors should review the assembled site to confirm all modules appear in the correct sequence and are accessible.
Consistent navigation reduces learner frustration and supports a smooth, uninterrupted learning experience.

Topics.Title: Keeping the Course Website Current
Topics.Summary: Covers best practices and workflows for re-publishing and maintaining an up-to-date course website as module content evolves over time.

Elements.Title: Understanding Why Re-Publishing Is Necessary
Elements.BodyText: Each time module content changes, the HTML index for that module must be refreshed before the course website accurately reflects those updates.
Elements.Notes: Think of the HTML index as a snapshot of the module at a given point in time; without re-publishing, visitors see outdated content.

Items.Text: PreseMaker's publish feature regenerates each module's HTML index to incorporate the latest content changes.
Skipping re-publication after edits means the live website will display stale or incorrect information.
Re-publishing ensures that the browsable site and each module's landing page stay synchronized with the source content.

Elements.Title: Identifying When to Re-Publish
Elements.BodyText: Knowing the right triggers for re-publishing helps maintain a consistently accurate course website without unnecessary extra work.
Elements.Notes: Establishing a checklist of change types that require re-publishing can reduce the risk of accidentally leaving the site out of date.

Items.Text: Re-publish whenever text, media, or structural changes are made to any module within the course.
Additions or removals of entire modules require a full site re-publish so the navigation and index reflect the new structure.
Minor cosmetic or metadata updates may also necessitate re-publishing if they affect the generated HTML index.

Elements.Title: The Re-Publishing Workflow in PreseMaker
Elements.BodyText: Re-publishing a course website in PreseMaker follows the same core steps as the initial publish, ensuring each module's HTML index is rebuilt before the site is assembled.
Elements.Notes: Consistently following the same workflow each time reduces errors and ensures no module is accidentally left un-refreshed.

Items.Text: Open the course in PreseMaker and navigate to the publish feature to begin the update process.
PreseMaker refreshes each module's HTML index during the publish run, capturing all recent content changes.
Once all module indexes are regenerated, the full browsable website is rebuilt and ready for distribution.

Elements.Title: Managing Multiple Modules During Updates
Elements.BodyText: Courses with several modules require careful coordination to ensure every changed module is re-published and no landing page is left outdated.
Elements.Notes: Maintaining a simple log of which modules were edited and when can streamline the re-publishing process for large courses.

Items.Text: Track which modules have been modified since the last publish to target only those that need refreshing.
Re-publishing the entire course at once is the safest approach when multiple modules have been updated simultaneously.
Verify each module's HTML index after publishing to confirm the latest content is correctly reflected on its landing page.

Elements.Title: Verifying the Updated Course Website
Elements.BodyText: After re-publishing, a review step confirms that all changes appear correctly across the live course website and each module's landing page.
Elements.Notes: Spot-checking a sample of recently edited content in a browser helps catch any publishing errors before learners encounter them.

Items.Text: Browse the regenerated site to confirm that updated module content is visible and accurate.
Check each affected module's HTML index page to ensure it serves as a correct and complete landing page.
Look for broken links, missing media, or layout issues that may have been introduced during the re-publish process.

Elements.Title: Establishing a Maintenance Cadence
Elements.BodyText: Setting a regular schedule or clear policy for re-publishing keeps the course website reliably current without requiring ad hoc decisions each time content changes.
Elements.Notes: For courses under active development, a publish-on-save or end-of-session habit can prevent the site from falling behind the source content.

Items.Text: Define a publishing cadence—such as after every editing session or at the end of each development sprint—to build consistency.
Communicate the update schedule to stakeholders so they know when to expect the live site to reflect recent changes.
Periodic full re-publishes, even without major edits, can catch any drift between source content and the published website.
